sense: people living together; the community at large

terms.gloss: society: the fellowship of people living together
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.53: gradūs autem plūrēs sunt societātis hominum
Cic. Amic. 20: societās generis hūmānī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: fellowship, community, society, implying union for a common purpose. Cicero speaks of societās hominum or generis hūmānī, human society, in widening circles from the family (Off. 1.53–54).

terms.gloss: society as an organized community of citizens
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.53: interius etiam est ejusdem esse cīvitātis
terms.comment: The society one belongs to as a citizen (see state, a country).

phrases.latin: Gradūs autem plūrēs sunt societātis hominum.
prīma societās in ipsō conjugiō est, proxima in līberīs, deinde ūna domus, commūnia omnia
phrases.english: the first society is marriage itself, the next is children, then one household with everything shared
